motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the consent agenda, removing Items 11.D. and 12.A. from the consent agenda and placing them as scheduled items for further discussion, and adding November 5 and December 16 to the 2025 City Council Meeting Schedule. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda and two added 2025 meeting dates
motions.summary: The council passed its consent agenda, pulled two items out for separate discussion, and added November 5 and December 16 to the 2025 meeting calendar.
motions.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents, beyond two more council meeting dates on next year's calendar if you plan to attend or comment.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Consenting to the Transfer of Title to Property Located in the Boundary of the Interlocal of the New School District in West Utah County.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Consenting to the Transfer of Title to Property Located in the Boundary of the Interlocal of the New School District in West Utah County with the following changes: 1. The language is changed from “purchase a new parcel” to “purchase a replacement parcel,” and 2. The consent is conditioned on the purchase of a replacement parcel for the elementary school. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Land transfer allowed only if school site is replaced
motions.summary: The city consented to a property transfer inside the new west Utah County school district's boundary, but only on the condition that a replacement parcel is bought for the elementary school.
motions.impact: The condition is the point: the city signed off only if a replacement site for the planned elementary school is purchased. If you are counting on that school, the city has tied its consent to keeping a site for it.

motions.item_title: Approve the Eagle Crest Storage site plan
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Eagle Crest Storage site plan. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Eagle Crest Storage site plan approved
motions.summary: The council approved the site plan for Eagle Crest Storage, clearing the layout for the project to move ahead.
motions.impact: If you live near the site, expect a storage facility to be built there. For the rest of the city, nothing changes.

motions.item_title: Set an end time of 10:30 PM for the meeting
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to set an end time of 10:30 PM for the meeting. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Set a 10:30 PM end time for the meeting
motions.summary: The council agreed to stop the meeting at 10:30 PM.
motions.impact: Purely procedural — nothing changes for residents. It only means items still on the agenda at 10:30 would have to wait for another meeting.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approving a Master Development Agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approving a Master Development Agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision.
motions.outcome: died for a lack of a second.
motions.headline: Rose Ranch agreement without the water conditions
motions.summary: A version of the Rose Ranch development agreement without the added water-rights conditions was put forward but went no further.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents. This was an alternate version of the same Rose Ranch agreement; the version with the water conditions attached is the one that governs.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approving a Master Development Agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision with the following conditions: 1. The last sentence in 6.2.3 under Water Rights is removed; and 2. Instruct staff to continue negotiations with the developer to come up with a take- down schedule for the water, should the developer enter into the agreement
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approving a Master Development Agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision with the following conditions: 1. The last sentence in 6.2.3 under Water Rights is removed; and 2. Instruct staff to continue negotiations with the developer to come up with a take- down schedule for the water, should the developer enter into the agreement. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion. Discussion ensued to clarify the conditions of the motion.
motions.headline: Rose Ranch subdivision agreement approved
motions.summary: The council approved the master development agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision, striking one sentence on water rights and directing staff to keep negotiating a schedule for delivering that water.
motions.impact: This sets the ground rules for a new subdivision, so expect construction there under the terms of this agreement. The water piece is not finished — staff are still working out when the developer hands water over.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 13.20.250 Developments within the City, Regarding Residential Water Rights Requirements
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 13.20.250 Developments within the City, Regarding Residential Water Rights Requirements. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Change to water rights required from new homes
motions.summary: The council changed the code section setting how much water rights a developer must hand over to the city before building homes here.
motions.impact: This lands on developers, not on you directly. What a builder must supply in water rights affects the cost of new homes and how much water the city banks for future growth.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 13.75 Eagle Mountain City Storm Water Ordinance
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 13.75 Eagle Mountain City Storm Water Ordinance. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Storm water rules updated
motions.summary: The council amended the city's storm water ordinance, the chapter of code governing how rain and runoff are handled.
motions.impact: Mostly affects builders and developers, who must meet the city's drainage requirements. Day to day, nothing changes for existing homeowners.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code to Enact Chapter 17.46 Transfer of Development Rights Overlay Zone
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code to Enact Chapter 17.46 Transfer of Development Rights Overlay Zone. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New rules to move development rights between sites
motions.summary: The council created a Transfer of Development Rights overlay zone, a new chapter of city code letting building rights be shifted from one piece of land to another.
motions.impact: This is a tool for landowners and developers, not something you use directly. Over time it can steer building away from land the city wants left open and toward areas it would rather see grow.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fourth Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fourth Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Fourth budget adjustment of the year
motions.summary: The council approved the fourth amendment to the city's 2024-2025 budget, shifting money between accounts partway through the fiscal year.
motions.impact: Routine mid-year bookkeeping — nothing changes for residents. Cities amend the budget several times a year as actual spending and revenue come in different from the original estimates.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting an Amended Water Conservation and Management Plan for Eagle Mountain City
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting an Amended Water Conservation and Management Plan for Eagle Mountain City. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Updated water conservation plan adopted
motions.summary: The council adopted a revised Water Conservation and Management Plan, the document setting out how Eagle Mountain plans to manage and stretch its water supply.
motions.impact: Nothing changes at your tap today. This is the planning document the city has to keep current, and any actual watering rules or rates would come later as separate decisions.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Consolidated Fee Schedule, Section 9 Ordinance Enforcement Fines, Section 13 Building Department, Section 16 Sewer Rates, and Section 17 Storm Water
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Consolidated Fee Schedule, Section 9 Ordinance Enforcement Fines, Section 13 Building Department, Section 16 Sewer Rates, and Section 17 Storm Water. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Fee changes for sewer, storm water, and building
motions.summary: The city updated its fee schedule covering code enforcement fines, building department fees, sewer rates, and storm water charges. The motion itself does not list the new amounts.
motions.impact: Sewer and storm water charges appear on your monthly utility bill, and building fees hit anyone pulling a permit. The motion does not say how much each changed, so check the adopted fee schedule for figures.

motions.item_title: Remove two items from the Legislative Priorities List related to establishing discontinued zoni…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to remove two items from the Legislative Priorities List related to establishing discontinued zoning and the transfer of development rights ordinances. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Drop two zoning items from the city's priority list
motions.summary: The council removed two items — discontinued zoning and transfer of development rights — from the Legislative Priorities List it uses to guide its own agenda.
motions.impact: This is housekeeping on an internal to-do list, so nothing changes for residents. The transfer-of-development-rights rules were adopted the same night, so that item no longer needed to be pending.
